body.p: Subject matter from former Claim 13 that was rejected as being anticipated by figure 3B and paragraphs 62, 65, and 72 of Ye now appears in Claim 8.

The arguments that persuaded the examiner to allow claims 1-7 are believed to apply to why Claim 8 should now be allowed. The instant specification explains that a video can be transformed using ML "to avoid rendering multiple viewpoints simultaneously" whereas Ye does precisely what Applicant, and the instant claims, avoid in that Ye uses ML merely to select which of plural pre-existing camera views (i.e., video streams) to present to a person.

In paragraph 62, Ye agrees with Applicant's summary above by explaining that figure 3B illustrates camera views (plural) capturing the different actions are streamed to the passive spectator and the streaming of each camera view correlates with the occurrence of different actions within the video game. These camera views "are part of a recommendation stream provided to the passive spectator." Figure 3B illustrates this.

Paragraph 65 of Ye explicitly states that "the view recommendation engine also receives the various camera views generated from game play data 308 of game 1" and that the output of the recommendation engine "is used "to select [not transform] specific one of the camera views."
Paragraph 72 of Ye further makes Applicant's case: "The feature processing engine 401 extracts the image data 311 from the image datastore 311 and processes the image data 311 to extract

various features of the images captured in each camera view of game play data". The ensuing paragraphs of Ye teach that these features are input to the recommendation engine along with spectator characteristics and preferences to enable the engine to "identifjy] the camera views to be provided to the passive spectator", e.g., paragraph 73.

Accordingly, because Ye teaches a ML model that identifies a preexisting camera view whereas Claim 8 as amended avoids rendering multiple viewpoints simultaneously by inputting only the PC video stream to the ML model and transforming the PC video stream to output the NPC video stream, Claim 8 is patentable.

Similarly, because Claim 15 inputs the first video to a ML model and does not input the second video from the viewpoint of the second character not controllable by a player to the ML model but nonetheless produces the second video, it too is patentable.

For completeness, these claims require the first screen render to be sent from a cloud server to at least one display for presentation of the first screen render at a first time and actions of NPCs to be delayed for at least one frame while the ML model generates the second screen render. The rejection cites paragraphs 49, 16, and 54 (in the order listed in the Office Action) but these paragraphs do not say what the examiner alleges they say. Paragraph 16 of Ye teaches nothing more relevant than re-executing the video game to generate the active spectator camera view. Paragraph 49 teaches nothing more relevant than a video game being executed locally at client devices and metadata from the executing video game being transmitted to a game cloud server. Paragraph 54 merely states at its

most relevant that a game engine manages the game logic of the game, collects and transmits inputs to the game logic, and manages the allocation and synchronization of the functional portions of the game engine to render the game. Nowhere in this relied-upon subject matter is there any mention of sending a first screen render from a cloud server for presentation of the first screen render at a first time while delaying actions of NPCs for at least one frame while the ML model generates the second screen render. Nothing of the sort appears in the relied-upon subject matter.

Any and all amendments are without prejudice or acquiescence in anything the examiner has placed on the record other than admissions favorable to Applicant including admissions of allowable subject matter. Although this paper may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or references of record, Applicant does not concede that any previously pending claim is not patentable over the references of record. Instead, any alterations or characterizations herein are made to expedite prosecution of the instant application. Applicant preserves the right to pursue additional claims that encompass any subject matter supported by the instant specification, including subject matter that may be found to have been disclaimed in this or any other related application. With this in mind, no inference is to be drawn from review of this or any related application that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the instant application. To the extent that any estoppel-driven disclaimers or disavowals of subject matter are considered to have occurred in any prior paper in this or any related application, they are hereby rescinded, and the examiner is invited to reconsider the instant claims in light of the references of record. The examiner is cordially invited to telephone the undersigned for any reason that would advance the instant application to allowance.
